It is intuitively not surprising that it is detrimental to use self-loops. When the loss function penalizes monochromatic edges, the messages passed from a vertex to its neighbors during message-passing tell each neighbor to not be the same color as the vertex. Therefore, self-loops being introduced may result in vertices telling themselves not to be their own color, which could confuse the optimizer and make it think there is no good color to assign each vertex.
